title: BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.setNudgeStreamer is the only one of six streamer setters with no zero-address guard — zeroing it silently strands every accrued stream while batchMint keeps succeeding
description: All six donor contracts reject `setNudgeStreamer(address(0))` with an explicit guard — BalancerPoolerV2.sol:247, Uniboost.sol:191, NudgeRatchet.sol:106, PromotionUniV2_Eth.sol:349, StableYieldAccumulator.sol:514. `BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.setNudgeStreamer` (:299-302) has none, because address(0) is its deliberate 'streaming disabled' sentinel: `batchMint` gates the whole `pullPendingStream` loop on `if (_nudgeStreamer != address(0))` (:538). The sentinel design is defensible in isolation; the hazard is that it is the ONE setter in a family of six that accepts the value every sibling rejects, and its failure mode is silent while every sibling's is a loud revert.
impact: An operator wiring the sink from a wrong or placeholder address (see DEV-06) gets no error and no event distinguishable from a normal reconfiguration. batchMint continues to succeed. Every accrued stream stays stranded in the streamer and the batcher is paid only whatever was already sitting in the sink. Because `pullPendingStream` is the ONLY path by which streamed funds reach the batch minter, and donors keep pushing INTO the streamer, the divergence grows without bound and is visible only by comparing streamer buffers against sink balances. This inverts the intuition an operator would form from the five guarded siblings.
attackPath: 1. Operator wires the sink using a wrong or placeholder address. The trigger is present IN-REPO, not hypothesised: server/deployments/mainnet-addresses.ts:131 carries `NudgeStreamer: 0x000...000`, type-indistinguishable from a real address because the ContractAddresses interface is regenerated from ANVIL data with every field a required plain `string` (DEV-06).

2. BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.setNudgeStreamer (top-level HEAD :290-293) accepts address(0) with no guard - unlike all five siblings, which revert (BalancerPoolerV2:247, Uniboost:191, PromotionUniV2_Eth:349, StableYieldAccumulator:514, NudgeRatchet:106). Verified directly at HEAD this run.
3. batchMint gates the whole pullPendingStream loop on `if (_nudgeStreamer != address(0))` (:527), so the streaming leg becomes a silent no-op while the mint itself keeps succeeding.

4. Donors continue to push into the streamer. Every accrued stream strands. Nothing reverts, nothing logs a distinguishable event, and the five loud siblings have taught the operator to expect a revert on a bad address.
evidence: PoC workspace/phoenix-phase-2-staging/test/AuditDevStreamerWiring.t.sol, run with --fork-url against the live local chain — 2/2 PASS. test_zeroAddressGuardAsymmetry: all six donors return ok==false for setNudgeStreamer(address(0)); BatchNFTMinterMultiToken returns ok==true and nudgeStreamer() reads address(0). test_zeroedSinkStrandsAccruedStreams: with the streamer wired, a qualifying batchMint(26) pays the batcher 45,045,015 USDC + 5,000e18 phUSD + 50,000e18 Kendu; with the streamer zeroed the SAME batchMint SUCCEEDS with no revert and no event and pays 189,464 USDC + 0 phUSD + 0 Kendu, leaving the full matured pot stranded in the streamer.
recommendation: Either (a) emit a distinct, unambiguous event when the streamer is set to zero (e.g. `NudgeStreamingDisabled`) so the disable is loud in logs, or (b) add an explicit `setNudgeStreamingEnabled(bool)` and require a non-zero address in `setNudgeStreamer`, separating 'disable' from 'misconfigure'. At minimum, the mainnet script must post-assert `batchMinter.nudgeStreamer() == <expected>` after the call — DeployMocks post-asserts only the SYA leg (:1129) of seven such calls.

classification.c4Criterion: C4 Medium - 'Assets not at direct risk, but the function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted ... with stated assumptions, but external requirements'.
classification.assetImpact: No theft, no economic loss, and expressly NOT scored as a value leak (the nudge pot is funded by yield on protocol-owned capital, so a non-arriving payout is a functional failure, not an economic one). The impact is AVAILABILITY OF A PROMISED PAYOUT: with the streamer zeroed, a qualifying batchMint(26) that should pay 45,045,015 USDC + 5,000e18 phUSD + 50,000e18 Kendu instead pays 189,464 USDC + 0 + 0, and SUCCEEDS - no revert, no distinguishable event. The entire matured pot stays stranded in the streamer. Because pullPendingStream is the ONLY path by which streamed funds reach the batch minter while donors keep pushing INTO the streamer, the divergence grows without bound and is observable only by manually comparing streamer buffers against sink balances.

3. batchMint gates the whole pullPendingStream loop on `if (_nudgeStreamer != address(0))` (:527), so the streaming leg becomes a silent no-op while the mint itself keeps succeeding.

classification.likelihood: medium. Requires an operator misstep, but a SPECIFICALLY ENABLED one: the exact wrong value sits in the repo's own mainnet address book today, the type system hides it, and DEV-07 shows the prose in that same file inverts the deployed/not-deployed distinction for four other entries. Detection is manual and comparative, so the window is long.
classification.assumptions: (1) Non-malicious owner throughout - this is rated purely as a Law-3 footgun, never as a malicious-admin vector. (2) The operator wires the streamer to address(0) or to a wrong address, e.g. by sourcing it from mainnet-addresses.ts. (3) The address(0)-as-'streaming-disabled' sentinel is a deliberate and defensible design in isolation; the defect is that the ONE setter in a family of six that accepts the value every sibling rejects also fails SILENTLY.
classification.externalRequirements: An operator mis-wire, plus the absence of a post-deploy assertion. DeployMocks post-asserts only the SYA leg (:1129) of seven setNudgeStreamer calls (see DEV-09), so the runbook does not catch it either.

severityRationale: ESCALATED to MEDIUM against the auditor's proposed Low. Escalation is justified on five independent grounds, and I am deliberately explicit because overstatement is a documented rejection cause for this pipeline. (1) PROVEN, NOT ARGUED: PoC workspace/phoenix-phase-2-staging/test/AuditDevStreamerWiring.t.sol is 2/2 PASS run --fork-url against the live chain; test_zeroAddressGuardAsymmetry shows all six donors return ok==false while BatchNFTMinterMultiToken returns ok==true, and test_zeroedSinkStrandsAccruedStreams shows the SAME batchMint(26) silently paying 189,464 instead of the full pot. The magnitude is measured, not estimated. (2) THE DEFECT IS THE SILENCE, NOT THE SENTINEL. A sentinel that disables a feature is fine; a sentinel that is accepted by exactly one of six sibling setters, whose five peers all revert loudly, actively INVERTS the intuition the operator has been trained to hold. That is the textbook Law-3 test - a competent, non-malicious owner would be surprised - and Law 3 requires such a footgun to be classified BY THE IMPACT IT UNLOCKS, not auto-downgraded to a centralization/QA note. The impact unlocked is the unbounded non-arrival of the entire nudge pot. (3) THE TRIGGER IS LIVE IN-REPO. This is not 'an operator might one day fat-finger an address'. DEV-06 puts a 0x0 NudgeStreamer placeholder into mainnet-addresses.ts that the type system cannot distinguish from a real address, and DEV-07 shows the surrounding prose already inverts real-vs-placeholder for four other entries. The C4 'user input mistake' exclusion does not fire, because the repo itself supplies the wrong input. (4) FAMILY PRECEDENT. The identical class - a sentinel/zero collaborator making the value leg a silent no-op while the main call keeps succeeding - was filed in yield-claim-nft as c91bef813d (M-04) at MEDIUM, and the owner triaged it 'Owner ack - WILL FIX (revert on unwired dispatch)'. That fix landed on ATokenDispatcherV2; BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.setNudgeStreamer never received the fail-closed treatment. Rating the same class Low here would be inconsistent with the family's own accepted precedent. yield-claim-nft 563df2e64a (L-09) is the precedent for keeping a reborn instance open on its own rather than folding it under a fixed sibling. (5) PROPAGATES-TO-MAINNET, on the live BatchNFTMinterMultiToken, with no compensating on-chain or runbook control. NOT ESCALATED FURTHER TO HIGH: nothing is stolen, no attacker exists, the funds remain in the streamer rather than leaving the protocol, and re-pointing setNudgeStreamer to the correct address restores the pull path - the condition is recoverable once detected. It also requires an operator misstep, which bars the 'no hand-wavy hypotheticals' High bar. Medium is the ceiling this evidence supports. SCOPE DISCIPLINE - DO NOT CONFLATE: the adjacent _dispatch path is NOT part of this finding and is NOT part of the escalation basis. There a DonationSkipped event IS emitted and USDS re-sweeps, making that path bounded QUIETNESS with no value consequence. The escalation rests solely on the setNudgeStreamer leg, which is silent AND strands.
severityAgreement: DISAGREE - ESCALATED from proposed low to medium
classifierNotes: NOT related on root cause to phoenix-nft-staking 858e9e807a (H-01, wont-fix): that is the value-blind nudge GATE which OVER-pays the pot; DEV-03 STRANDS it - economically the opposite direction. The 858e9e80 wont-fix is NOT cited against this finding. Minimum remediation: emit a distinct NudgeStreamingDisabled event, or split disable from misconfigure via setNudgeStreamingEnabled(bool) + require non-zero; and post-assert `batchMinter.nudgeStreamer() == <expected>` in the mainnet script.

parkedItemsCarriedForward.title: ERC4626YieldStrategy.previewRedeem / previewDeposit view passthroughs still STATICCALL the underlying vault — the story-060 / YS-01 Tokemak fix is one-directional
parkedItemsCarriedForward.sourceVerification: Read against the TOP-LEVEL submodule HEAD lib/reflax-yield-vault (not a nested stale pin). :73-75 `return vault.previewDeposit(assets);` and :83-85 `return vault.previewRedeem(shares);`, both declared `external view` => Solidity emits STATICCALL. Twenty lines below, :110-115 credits principal via `vault.convertToAssets(sharesReceived)` with an in-source comment naming the exact hazard: 'Use convertToAssets (NOT previewRedeem): convertToAssets is ERC4626-mandated STATICCALL-safe, whereas some real vaults (e.g. Tokemak Autopools) mutate state inside previewRedeem and revert with StateChangeDuringStaticCall when called as an external view.' The authors therefore knew the hazard and hardened ONE call site.
parkedItemsCarriedForward.whyItMatters: Against a real Tokemak Autopool these two views revert for every caller, always; against MockAutoDOLA (plain un-overridden OZ ERC4626) they return a clean number, always. The local rig therefore reports green on the exact behaviour that already bricked this project's YS-swap suite. Blast radius today is UI/keeper reads (no first-party on-chain caller found), which is why this is parked for triage rather than asserted as a Medium.

secondaryGapsInTheSameMockSection: No maxRedeem/maxWithdraw check before `vault.redeem` in _disposeShares (:128-135): against a real Autopool with a liquid reserve below the request, user withdrawals brick. Locally impossible to reproduce.

MockAutoDOLA._updateYield() mints assets into the vault BEFORE super._deposit mints shares, so convertToAssets(sharesReceived) > amount and creditedPrincipal at :115 can EXCEED the deposited amount — the precise opposite of that line's stated intent. Any local invariant asserting 'principal is never over-credited' passes VACUOUSLY. Flagged because a vacuous-harness result is a known repeat failure mode in this repo.
